AI mob moves from recordings of people
======================================

The moves AI mobs play from recordings of people (src/main/resources/assets/ntmgunfeel/animations/bot_moves.json:
turns on the spot, starts into a run, stops from one, down into a crouch from a walk or a run and up out of it into
one; bot_people.animation.json: a grenade's throw, a forward roll; bot_gaits.animation.json: runs, sprints and walks
ahead, walks aside and back with the gun up) are put on the AI mobs' model (Minecraft's humanoid, its arms and legs
cut at the elbow and the knee: ten parts) by tools/motion/retarget_moves.py, retarget_crouch.py and moves_to_mod.py,
retarget_actions.py and actions_to_mod.py, retarget_mocap.py and gaits_to_mod.py:

  100STYLE by Ian Mason
    https://www.ianxmason.com/100style/  https://zenodo.org/records/8127870
    I. Mason, S. Starke, T. Komura. Real-Time Style Modelling of Human Locomotion via Feature-Wise Transformations
    and Local Motion Phases. Proc. ACM Comput. Graph. Interact. Tech. 5, 1 (2022).
    StartStop_FW, Swat_TR1, Swat_FW, Swat_SR, Swat_BR, Neutral_FW
    License: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0)
             https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

  CMU Graphics Lab Motion Capture Database
    http://mocap.cs.cmu.edu/
    The data used in this project was obtained from mocap.cs.cmu.edu. The database was created with funding from
    NSF EIA-0196217.
    Subjects 9 (09_06), 16 (16_45, 16_46, 16_56, 16_57), 69 (69_14), 78 (78_06), 79 (79_35), 104 (104_53, 104_55,
    104_56, 104_57), 127 (127_06, 127_08), 128 (128_11), 139 (139_10), 143 (143_02, 143_03)
    Terms: free for all uses; the data itself may not be resold, even converted.

  Open Motion Project by ACCAD/The Ohio State University
    https://accad.osu.edu/research/motion-lab/mocap-system-and-data
    Female1_B24_WalkToCrouch, Female1_C26_RunToCrouch, Female1_B25_CrouchToWalk, Female1_C27_CrouchToRun1
    License: Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported (CC BY 3.0)
             https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/

The recordings were changed: put on the mod's ten parts, each foot down kept standing on the floor in the mob's
frame for the turn or the way the move was made with, the legs only kept, keys thinned, and a turn to one side
mirrored for the other. The throw: the upper body only, a short piece of the swing, the head kept at the eye. The
runs and sprints: one step of both legs looped, the legs only, under hips held at one height, each foot down kept on
the floor and moved out to its own side (people's feet run nearly on one line), the knees straight ahead; some with
the steps made longer. The walks the same, slower; the walk aside (Swat_SR) the same, mirrored for the other side.
The ways down into a crouch and up out of it: the legs only, a piece from the walk or the run to the squat (or from
the squat to the walk or the run), the hips going down or up as the mod's crouch does over its first fifth of a
second, each foot down kept on the floor, the knees straight ahead, the feet apart; each mirrored for the other foot.
The forward roll: the whole body from the dive (the trunk bent a quarter turn forward) to the hips coming up again,
squeezed to the mob's roll and stretched to its way (the way past the person's put where no leg is down), lifted
where it would go into the floor.
